verdicts.strongest_argument: The arithmetic is correct in every particular — I verified it independently. FY26 guide is adj EBITDA $685-705mm (Q3 FY26 release, 2026-06-09), 39-week actual is $529mm, so the implied Q4 is exactly $156-176mm; Q4 FY25 adj EBITDA was $116mm and the company said the cyberattack cut it by 'approximately $50 million' in that same quarter. So the claim is right, and it is right entirely out of two documents the company published and the trade press headlined. Modern Distribution Management ran the headline 'UNFI Says Cyberattack Cost is up to $400M in Sales, $50M in EBITDA' on the FY25 Q4 print. The easy-comp structure is already in consensus: Zacks has Q4 EPS at $0.62 against a prior-year loss of $0.11 — the street is modelling the swing off the cyber-depressed base, which is only possible if it has already re-based the comparison. The FY28 $800mm target and the 'low-double-digit average annual adjusted EBITDA growth FY25-FY28' framing the claim leans on were published at the December 2025 Investor Day. This is a re-statement of published guidance plus a subtraction the sell-side cannot avoid doing, which is the 90-100 anchor softened only by the fact that nobody has written the 'underlying is zero, so FY27 is at risk' sentence out loud in preview copy. If anything the claim understates itself — using the confirmed $50mm rather than the $40-50mm estimate range, cyber-clean Q4 growth is -6% to +6%, midpoint zero, not +3%.

prior_publication.what_it_says: FY26 outlook adj EBITDA $685-705M and 39-week adj EBITDA $529M — the two numbers that produce the $156-176M implied Q4 the claim rests on.
Trade-press headline quantifying the cyberattack at up to $400M of sales and $50M of adjusted EBITDA, i.e. the add-back is public and headlined, not buried.
Investor Day sets ~$33bn sales and ~$800mm adjusted EBITDA for FY28 with low-double-digit average annual EBITDA growth — the FY27 waypoint the claim reverse-engineers.
Consensus Q4 EPS $0.62 vs prior-year -$0.11, showing the street already prices the cyber-distorted base.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The stock fell 10.28% on 2026-06-09, the day this guide was published, and is -20.88% from its 52-week high. The market's reaction to the very document this claim reads has already happened, and the 12.51% implied move with a +6.97-point put skew says it is braced for the FY27 guide to disappoint.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A published sell-side or press piece showing consensus FY27 adj EBITDA materially above $760mm — i.e. that the street has NOT re-based off the cyber-clean run-rate — would move this down toward 45.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every figure checks out against the PBS piece (42.2m May-2025, 36.6m May-2026, >13%, Arizona -55% April-to-April, Florida -22%, CBO's 2030 level reached in 2026) — but that piece is an AP wire story that ran on PBS, ABC News, NBC Washington, KSAT, Newser, Yahoo and Food Manufacturing on 2026-08-21, and Grocery Dive published a dedicated state-by-state SNAP-participation piece for the grocery-industry audience. This is national wire copy, not an obscure dataset. More damaging: UNFI's own CEO said on the 2026-06-09 call that 'the reduction in SNAP funding is beginning to make an impact or continuing to make an impact,' so the company has already told the market the headwind exists and has already embedded its view of it in the guide. The unpublished increment is only the elasticity — nobody has multiplied 47%-of-sales by a SNAP-dollar decline. That increment is real but modest: SNAP is roughly 8-9% of US grocery dollars, a 13% enrollment fall is maybe a 1% headwind to the exposed channel, and UNFI is a wholesaler whose Conventional volume is one step removed and largely pass-through.

prior_publication.what_it_says: SNAP enrollment fell from 42.2m in May 2025 to 36.6m in May 2026, faster than CBO projected, with Arizona -55% and Florida -22%.
Grocery-trade coverage of exactly where SNAP participation has fallen most, i.e. the read-across was delivered to the industry audience.
CEO on UNFI's own Q3 FY26 call: 'The reduction in SNAP funding is beginning to make an impact,' driving value-seeking behaviour among lower-income consumers.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: UNFI traded $47.90-48.58 in the second week of August and closed at $43.93 on 2026-09-04 — roughly -9% — with run_up_20d at -6.65% and run_up_5d at -4.08%. The SNAP wire ran on 2026-08-21, inside that window. Something consumer-shaped has been sold, and this is the most plausible candidate alongside diesel.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that UNFI's Conventional customer base is disproportionately SNAP-weighted with a quantified elasticity — or a state-level overlay onto UNFI's distribution footprint — published nowhere, would justify a 30.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both legs verify: NGVC daily-average comps +1.2% on a +3.1% basket with transaction count -1.8% and gross margin 29.9%→29.3%, and Sprouts Q2 comps -1.0%. But Sprouts is a $6bn+ company whose comp print on 2026-07-30 was covered by Grocery Dive, Supermarket News, TipRanks, Shelby Report and every wire, and 'natural-channel demand is cooling / traffic is negative' is one of the most widely told grocery narratives of 2026. That is the definition of a story already in the sector's price. The claim is also selectively read: NGVC's comp *accelerated* from +0.5% in Q2 to +1.2% in Q3, and Sprouts still grew sales 5% and beat on EPS — the release attributes the comp decline to lapping a prior-year produce surge, not to demand collapse. Negative transaction count with positive basket is the standard 2026 grocery signature and is not specific to the natural channel. And this is the same underlying document as UNFI-b#1: one NGVC release, cited twice from two URLs.

prior_publication.what_it_says: NGVC Q3 FY26: net sales +1.8% to $334.7m, daily-average comps +1.2% (basket +3.1%, transaction count -1.8%), gross margin 29.3% vs 29.9%.
Sprouts Q2 2026 sales up, comparable sales down 1% — trade-press headline treatment of the exact datapoint.
Grocery Dive coverage of Sprouts' Q2 with the CEO on performance and traffic headwinds.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: 20-day run-up of -6.65% brackets the 2026-08-06 NGVC print; the Sprouts print (2026-07-30) sits just before the 20-day window and UNFI is -20.88% from its 52-week high. Sector demand softness is being paid for, not discovered.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If UNFI's Natural segment growth is shown to be share gain from a specific customer win rather than channel demand, the read-across breaks and the finding becomes irrelevant rather than priced.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I verified the numbers exactly against the Amazon exhibit: physical stores $5,794m vs $5,595m, '4%' and '4%' ex-FX, with the March-2026 quarter at $5,785m. The claim is factually clean. It is also lifted verbatim from the single most-read earnings document of the quarter, published 2026-07-30 and parsed line-by-line by thousands of analysts within minutes, and the Whole Foods concentration it depends on is a standing disclosure in UNFI's 10-K. The information content is close to nil in any case: the finding says the largest customer's growth is *unchanged*, which is the null hypothesis. A datapoint whose content is 'no change' cannot be a mispricing however obscure the read-across; and physical stores is Amazon's Whole Foods plus Fresh plus Go, so it is a noisy proxy that does not isolate UNFI's actual customer.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Physical stores net sales of $5,794m for the June 2026 quarter vs $5,595m prior year, +4% and +4% ex-FX.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No move in UNFI attributable to 2026-07-30 is identifiable; the 20-day run-up window starts after it. Consistent with a datapoint the market treated as non-news, which is the point.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A sharp break in the physical-stores line — an acceleration or a drop to flat — rather than a continuation, would make this worth 20 instead of 78.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The pull-forward is real and I confirmed the prior pattern: FY24 Q4 reported 2024-10-01 and FY25 Q4 reported 2025-09-30, against 2026-09-08 for a fiscal year ended 2026-08-01 — 38 days versus roughly 59. But the fact itself is not obscure at all: it went out on Business Wire on 2026-08-10 and was carried by Yahoo Finance, StockTitan, Zacks and the earnings calendars, and it is the single date every holder of this option chain is trading around. What is unpublished is only the inference, and the inference is weak in both directions and arguably backwards: 38 days is exactly the lag UNFI already runs on Q1-Q3 (Q3 ended 2026-05-02, reported 2026-06-09 — 38 days), so the change normalises Q4 onto the existing cadence rather than creating an anomaly. The baseline's own plausibility check reads 'fits_cadence, 91 days against a 91-day cadence.' Scheduling signal is also sign-ambiguous — the literature cuts toward early reporters having good news, so a hunter using this as a warning is arguing against its own prior.

prior_publication.what_it_says: UNFI will report its 13-week fiscal 2026 fourth quarter on the morning of Tuesday, September 8, 2026, with a call at 8:30 a.m. ET.
The prior-year comparison point: FY24 Q4 was released 2024-10-01, establishing the late-September/early-October pattern the claim measures against.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No identifiable move on 2026-08-10 — the stock was still around $47.90-48.58 in the days after. The market absorbed the date change as administrative, which is either the mispricing or the correct reading, and nothing in the tape distinguishes them.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A concrete reason for the pull-forward — a scheduled refinancing, a strategic announcement, or a same-day investor event — would give the signal a sign and take this to 20.

verdicts.strongest_argument: All four items sit in a single press release that UNFI issued and filed as exhibit 99.1 to an 8-K on 2026-07-09 — I read it: Tarditi to President/COO, Luchini from Carrier as CFO effective 2026-08-10, Bushway departing 2027-01-01. Not a discovery in a footnote; a company-issued announcement, wire-distributed, and picked up in the August trade and financial press summaries of UNFI leadership. 'A CFO four weeks in the seat sets the first multi-year guide' is a real and reasonable risk, but it is a heuristic every buy-side desk applies automatically the moment a CFO change is announced eight weeks before a guide date — that is the textbook definition of structural-and-known. The Echols item is immaterial: a Chief Corporate Affairs Officer does not touch the EBITDA guide. UNFI-b#2 is the same document and the same thesis; this should not be counted twice.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Company press release announcing Tarditi to President/COO, Martin to Chief Commercial Officer, Luchini as CFO effective 2026-08-10, and Bushway's departure 1 January 2027.
Financial-press coverage recapping the August 2026 UNFI leadership slate including Tarditi, Martin, Luchini and Bushway's exit.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No isolable move on 2026-07-09 or 2026-08-10 — the stock was still near $48 on 2026-08-12, well after both. The +6.97 put skew and 12.51% implied move do price an unusually wide guide outcome, which is the form this risk takes.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence the new CFO is presenting the FY27 guide himself and has signalled a re-baselining — or an unannounced further departure in finance — would take this to 30.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The diesel facts are exact — $5.599/gal for the week of 2026-08-31 and $4.578 on 2026-07-06 both verify — but that is the problem: US on-highway diesel rose 53.8% from early January to early August 2026, the largest January-to-August move in 32 years of weekly EIA data, driven by Strait of Hormuz disruption and Russia's export ban. This is front-page macro that has repriced every freight-intensive equity in the market, and the read-across from diesel to a private-fleet food distributor is the most obvious one there is. Worse for the claim, UNFI already told the market its position on 2026-06-09: fuel and transportation pressure is 'embedded' in Q4 guidance, and management named three mitigants — 'we hedge part of the fuel,' contractual protection (i.e. surcharges), and route optimisation. The genuinely unpublished increment is the $5m Level-2 balance from an XBRL R-page, and that increment carries a logical flaw: a $5m mark-to-market fair value tells you nothing about notional hedged volume, and in a violently rising diesel market a small positive MTM is as consistent with a decent hedge that has already been marked as with no hedge at all. The claim infers size from fair value. Third-party corroboration also cuts against novelty: Natural Grocers named 'higher freight costs' as a gross-margin driver in its 2026-08-06 release, so the freight-cost transmission is already visible in published documents.

prior_publication.what_it_says: National on-highway diesel average $5.599/gal for the week of 31 August 2026.
US on-highway diesel rose 53.8% from early January to early August 2026, the largest such move in 32 years of weekly EIA data, on Hormuz disruption and Russia's diesel export ban.
UNFI management on its own call: fuel and transportation pressure embedded in Q4 guidance, mitigated by partial hedging, contractual protection and route optimisation.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: UNFI fell from ~$48 in mid-August to $43.93 on 2026-09-04 while diesel held above $5.25, and realised 20-day vol is 28.8% with a +6.97-point 25-delta put skew on 1,789 contracts. The market has been paying for downside into this print over precisely the weeks diesel was making 32-year records.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A disclosed notional hedged volume (gallons or dollar notional, not fair value) showing coverage well under a third of consumption, plus evidence UNFI's customer contracts lack a fuel surcharge pass-through, would take this to 25.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the same document as UNFI-a#2 — the NGVC Q3 FY26 release of 2026-08-06 — read from the SEC exhibit instead of the IR page. Every number verifies (net sales +1.8% to $334.7m, transaction count -1.8%, gross margin 29.9%→29.3% on mix, shrink and freight, FY26 EPS guide $2.07-2.15→$2.07-2.11, comps 1.5-2.5%→1.5-2.0%) and the primary-distributor cyber distortion is in the release, along with a $2.0m business-interruption insurance gain. Two things blunt it. First, one factual error: the claim says NGVC's quarter sits 'entirely inside UNFI's Q4' — it does not. NGVC's quarter is 1 April to 30 June 2026; UNFI's Q4 is 3 May to 1 August. April falls in UNFI's Q3 and July is missing entirely, so the overlap is two of three months. Second, the magnitude: NGVC's total net sales are ~$1.3bn annualised, of which ~69% bought from UNFI is roughly $0.9bn, under 3% of UNFI's ~$31bn. A top-end-only guide trim at a customer worth 3% of revenue is not a print-moving fact on its own, and the 69% dependency has been an annual 10-K disclosure for years — age is not novelty. What survives is the channel read-across, and that is a shared story with the far more visible Sprouts print.

prior_publication.what_it_says: NGVC Q3 FY26 8-K exhibit with the comp, traffic, gross-margin and revised FY26 guidance figures, and the reference to the primary distributor's June/July 2025 cyber incident.
Same release redistributed on a retail-facing financial platform on the day, i.e. the document reached a broad audience.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The 2026-08-06 date sits at the front edge of the -6.65% 20-day run-up. NGVC's own reaction is where this news was primarily expressed; UNFI's subsequent drift is consistent with the channel signal having been absorbed.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If UNFI's Natural segment growth is shown to depend materially on NGVC-type independents rather than Whole Foods and larger accounts, the 3%-of-revenue objection weakens and this drops toward 30.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Four of the five changes are in one company-issued press release filed as exhibit 99.1 on 2026-07-09 — Tarditi, Martin, Luchini and Bushway are all named in it, which I confirmed by reading it — and the August financial press recapped the same slate. So the 'five changes in seven weeks' framing overstates the discovery: it is one announcement plus one Form 4. The genuine increment is the Echols exit disclosed only via a 2026-08-24 Form 4 with no 8-K, which is a legitimately obscure catch, and it is also the least material of the five: Chief Corporate Affairs Officer sits nowhere near the FY27 EBITDA guide, and a departure with no 8-K is consistent with the company's own view that it is not material — correctly, under Item 5.02, which only compels disclosure for named executive officers. This is the same document and the same thesis as UNFI-a#5 and should not be scored as two independent findings; the marginal information over a#5 is small, which is why this sits slightly lower rather than materially lower.

prior_publication.what_it_says: One press release covering Tarditi to President/COO, Martin to Chief Commercial Officer, Luchini as CFO effective 2026-08-10, and Bushway's 1 January 2027 departure — and it names Echols as continuing in role.
Press recap of the August 2026 UNFI leadership changes including the new CFO's 10 August start and Bushway's exit.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The stock was still around $48 on 2026-08-12, two days after the CFO started and a month after the announcement, so none of this was sold as news. What the baseline does price is guide uncertainty: 12.51% implied move on 90.9% ATM IV.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A further unannounced finance-organisation departure, or evidence the FY27 guide is being deferred to a later date, would take this to 25.

interactions: Substantial overlap, and it cuts the effective finding count from nine to about five. (1) UNFI-a#2 and UNFI-b#1 are the SAME document — Natural Grocers' Q3 FY26 release of 2026-08-06 — cited once from the IR page and once from the SEC exhibit. a#2's increment over b#1 is the Sprouts datapoint; b#1's increment over a#2 is the guidance trim and the 69% purchase concentration. Counted as two findings this double-weights one August grocery release worth under 3% of UNFI's revenue. The two also read the same document in opposite spirit: a#2 stresses negative traffic, b#1 stresses the guide cut, and neither mentions that NGVC's comp ACCELERATED from +0.5% to +1.2% or that low-end guidance was left untouched at $2.07 and 1.5%. (2) UNFI-a#5 and UNFI-b#2 are the SAME document — the 2026-07-09 8-K exhibit 99.1 — and the same thesis: a four-week-old CFO delivers the first FY27 guide. b#2's only genuinely new item over a#5 is the Echols Form 4, which is immaterial to earnings. These are one finding, not two. (3) a#0, a#5 and b#2 all resolve into a single trade: the FY27 guide is the swing factor and it is at risk. a#0 argues the run-rate cannot support it; a#5/b#2 argue the person setting it is new. Same downside, expressed three times, against one 12.51% implied move and one +6.97-point put skew that already pays for it. (4) a#1, a#2 and b#1 all resolve into 'consumer/channel demand is soft', and UNFI's own CEO put SNAP on the record as a headwind on 2026-06-09, before any of the three source documents. (5) b#0 is partly corroborated by b#1's own document — NGVC named higher freight costs in its gross-margin decline — which means the freight transmission b#0 treats as undiscovered is already visible in a published third-party release. FACTUAL FLAGS, separate from pricing: b#1's assertion that NGVC's quarter sits 'entirely inside UNFI's Q4' is wrong (1 April-30 June vs 3 May-1 August; April is in UNFI's Q3, July is absent). b#0 infers hedge NOTIONAL from a $5m fair-value MTM balance, which does not follow — a small positive mark in a fast-rising diesel market is consistent with several hedge sizes. a#0's arithmetic, by contrast, I reproduced exactly and it is if anything conservative: on the confirmed $50m cyber add-back the cyber-clean Q4 range is -6% to +6%, midpoint zero, not the +3% claimed. a#3's Amazon figures are exact to the dollar. a#1's SNAP figures are exact.  All nine claims lean bearish or neutral except a#3 and possibly a#4, so the set as a whole is arguing for the side the option skew has already bought.
